components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Tactile main action with a pressed burgundy edge.

components.name: Paper Button
components.description: Quiet secondary action on lightly textured paper.
components.css: .ds-button-paper { min-height: 44px; padding: 0 1.15em; border: 0; border-radius: 10px; color: var(--mm-color-ink); background: #fdf8ec var(--mm-tex-grain); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px rgb(60 42 28 / .5), 0 2px 0 rgb(60 42 28 / .28), 0 4px 8px -4px rgb(40 24 10 / .3); font: 650 15px/1.1 var(--mm-font-sans); cursor: pointer; transition: box-shadow 160ms ease, background-color 160ms ease; } .ds-button-paper:hover:not(:disabled) { background-color: var(--mm-color-fresh); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px rgb(60 42 28 / .72), 0 2px 0 rgb(60 42 28 / .32), 0 5px 10px -4px rgb(40 24 10 / .34); } .ds-button-paper:active:not(:disabled) { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px rgb(60 42 28 / .7); } .ds-button-paper:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--mm-color-burgundy-700); outline-offset: 4px; } .ds-button-paper:disabled { opacity: .55; cursor: not-allowed; }

narrative.overview:
Mori's Mix should feel like a well-used recipe book kept open on an oak kitchen table: personal, warm, tactile, and quietly playful. Parchment pages, a burgundy leather cover, paper tabs, brass details, and Mori's rat-chef identity make the journal recognizable without turning cooking tasks into decoration.

Materials do much of the storytelling; restraint protects the work. Oak and leather anchor the screen, paper carries reading and writing, and small stamps or handwritten notes add personality. Buttons and bookmarks can feel physical, while recipe text and fields stay calm and legible. Mori's companion repeats paper and sage in compact chat bubbles. AI-created recipes remain visibly reviewable as drafts, with saving presented as a separate, explicit action.
keyCharacteristics: Oak, leather, parchment, and kraft-paper surfaces with restrained grain.
Fraunces headings paired with Figtree interface text and occasional Caveat notes.
Burgundy for primary actions, sage for support, brass for hardware, and lilac for active AI Chef progress.
Soft paper lift, a deeper desk shadow, pressed button edges, physical bookmark tabs, and Mori's paper-and-sage chat bubbles.

rules.name: The Ledger Mark Rule
rules.body: Burgundy identifies the brand and primary actions; Garden Sage carries supporting actions and states; Antique Brass stays on hardware and small editorial accents; Lilac Paper marks AI Chef progress; Warm Parchment and Espresso Ink do most of the reading.

rules.name: The Two-Hand Rule
rules.body: Use Fraunces and Figtree for nearly all product text. Save Caveat for a short note or flourish where handwriting adds meaning.

rules.name: The Page-Layer Rule
rules.body: Give paper a soft ambient lift, reserve the deepest shadow for the journal on the desk, and use pressed edges for actions that should feel tactile.

dos: Do keep reading and writing surfaces warm and quiet: parchment backgrounds, Espresso Ink body text, and unobtrusive grain.
Do use Fraunces for editorial hierarchy, Figtree for functional copy, and Caveat only for short handwritten notes.
Do make primary actions burgundy and give controls a visible keyboard focus treatment.
Do let secondary controls and status accents take their own color role: Garden Sage for support, Antique Brass for hardware and small marks.
Do make AI drafts read as editable previews, and show the explicit save action as a separate confirmation step.
donts: Don't use Caveat for instructions, form labels, or long passages.
Don't put tape, paper clips, or stamps over a control or its text; they are decorative.
Don't let grain, stains, or shadow compete with recipe text; keep body content on high-contrast paper.
Don't present a generated recipe draft with the same saved state as an account-owned recipe before the cook confirms it.
